Ticket Id: 26905

Dr Jose Jiminez
Surgeon
Melbourne Private Hospital
19 Grange Road
Melbourne 3000

22/01/2007

RE: Mrs Ann Howard, DOB: 1971

Thank you for seeing Mrs Howard who presented with symptoms and signs suggestive of early stage of
intestinal obstruction. Your further assessment would be appreciated.

Mrs Howard is a 36-year-old married woman. She has a past history of ovarian cystectomy,
appendicectomy and spontanous abortion.                                                                        Commented [B1]: possible spontaneous

On 20/01/2007, she presented with a severe persistent lower abdominal pain. Her pain was more
prominent on the left side. Moreover, sitting up, walking or bending exacerbated her pain. No associated
symptoms were reported apart from similar pain one day ago which was relieved by Valium. On                    Commented [B2]: a
examination, the left lower quadrant of the abdomen was tender. An abdominal mass was palpable also.
Three days later, she reported mild improvement of the pain. However, there were no bowel movements
over the last 3 days except one time of hard stool mixed with bright blood.                                    Commented [B3]: passing

Today, she presented with a worsening pain following eating, associated with constipation and inability to     Commented [B4]: the
pass flatus. Examinations revealed a moderated tense abdomen as well as quit bowel sounds

In view of the above, my provisional diagnosis is early stage of intestinal obstruction. I suspect it may be
diverticulitis or carcinoma. I would appreciate your further evaluation and management as you see
suitable.

For any queries, please do not hesitate to contact me.

Yours sincerely,

Doctor
